name: construction-progress-bar
description: #1012: a construction site's progress bar must stay anchored to the site (the ghost mesh), not float above whichever worker is currently building it. Places a tier-1 living_quarters via real click-driven interaction (role: player, same known-flat (2,6) tile building-placement-visual.json already places living_quarters on), then drives a handful of ticks so a staffed roster member has walked over and started work -- landing mid-in_progress, ghost still present, no building yet -- and captures a screenshot at that checkpoint for the later visual-tester phase to judge the bar's anchor against. Does not assert anything about the bar itself: TaskProgressBar/GhostMesh are renderer-only (no __gameState field exposes bar position), so this file only proves the state a screenshot needs (an in-progress site with a claimed ghost) is reachable by real clicks -- the bar's actual on-screen anchor is a visual-channel judgement, not a scenario `expect`.

steps.description: Real click path: open the build panel, buy living_quarters, pick the known-flat (2,6) tile (building-placement-visual.json already places living_quarters there post-#1008's flatness check), confirm. Ordering only queues a construction site (blue ghost, #556) -- no building exists yet.

expect.note: Ordered, not placed: a construction site is queued, no building exists yet.

steps.description: Mid-construction checkpoint: a staffed roster member has had time to walk to (2,6) and start work, but the tier-1 base duration is nowhere near spent -- the site is genuinely mid-in_progress, not finished. This is the capture point the visual-tester phase judges the site-anchored bar against (#1012): the bar should sit on the ghost at (2,6), not float above wherever the builder happens to be standing. cameraFocus targets (2,6) at a close distance (matching the visual-tester's manual `--focus "2,6,6"` probe) so the world-space progress bar (0.6m x 0.08m) actually fills enough of the frame to be legible against the ghost's own shading, instead of the couple of pixels it renders as under the default wide top-down orbiting camera (#1012 visual-loop finding).

expect.note: Still under construction 10 ticks in -- proves this is a genuine mid-build snapshot.

steps.description: Drive the site to completion so a later run of this file can be extended to check the bar disappears once the building lands.
